## Introduction

[No abstract is needed.]  Each reproducibility project will have a straightforward, no frills report of the study and reproducibility results. These reports will be publicly available as supplementary material for the aggregate report(s) of the project as a whole.  Also, to maximize project integrity, the intro and methods will be written and critiqued in advance of your attempt to reproduce the results. Introductions can be just 1-2 paragraphs clarifying the main idea of the original study, the target finding for your reproducibility attempt, and any other essential information. ### Justification for choice of study

  De la Fuente et al. (2021) investigates how wild marmosets adjust their foraging partner choices and strength of foraging associations with their conspecifics under varied food availability. The authors manipulated the abundance and distribution of food resources to look at how the marmosets of different sex, hierarchy, and age interact with each other. Among many of their hypothesis, I would like to investigate H1b with a focus on node degree: social tolerance towards juveniles is high as juveniles would share a feeding site with a greater number of group members (other juveniles and adults). This hypothesis align with my broad research interest on marmoset development, focusing particularly how different parent-infant/helper-offspring interactions contribute to offspring behavioral and brain development. The social tolerance towards juveniles from this study can provide me with insights into the flexible sociality in marmosets. In addition, the study manipulates a large dataset, and simulating the data allows me to learn how to deal with huge database with a wide range of predictor variables. 

### Anticipated challenges

  I will simulate the individual dataset from the study and look at whether the model used in the study is robust by analyzing the age effect. Because the paper and supplement materials did not provide a complete statistic output, I will first refit the original GLMM (Response variable: node degree; Predictor variables: Age + Sex * Exp_con; Random effects: Groups ID + Daily sessions) with the original dataset. Next, I will simulate the data 1000 times while keeping all the original variables required from the H1b (Condition, Session, Group, Individual, Sex, Age) for each observation. For simulation, I will generate new node degree values (Animals_shared) by preserving the Sex * Exp_con effect and setting age effect = 0. Then, I will refit the original GLMM with the simulated data and check how often does the model report a significant age effect. Because the authors didn't provide the original code, the reconstructed models may not reproduce the exact original implementation.

### Learning goals

  This project is feasible because it includes stimulation only. I would like to gain in-depth coding skills with R on cleaning, simulating, and analyzing data. I would like to develop critical thinking skills on analyzing the robustness of models instead of simply accepting all the models and statistics presented by the researchers. I will also gain a deep understanding of GLMM so that I can readily use them in future projects.
